verdict_summary:
Adversarial result: 4 CONFIRMED, 6 PARTIAL, 2 REFUTED, plus 2 better sources the researcher missed. The lane's central conclusions survive; several of its citations do not.

Most damaging error (as predicted, it is a license claim): the Overture categories CSV. The researcher labelled it CDLA-Permissive-2.0 with attribution "(c) Overture Maps Foundation". Neither half is right. The CSV they downloaded sits in github.com/OvertureMaps/schema, which the GitHub API and the LICENSE file both report as CC-BY-4.0. And docs.overturemaps.org/attribution shows the Places DATA theme is a mix — CDLA-Permissive-2.0 for Meta/Microsoft/PinMeTo/Krick/RenderSEO/DAC/BrightQuery, Apache-2.0 for Foursquare ("Copyright 2024 Foursquare Labs, Inc. All rights reserved"), CC0-1.0 for AllThePlaces — with per-contributor attribution required. core.businesses must therefore record which provider each row came from.

Second refutation: the Overpass US count. Claimed 242 (64/178/0). Measured today: 272 (69 nodes, 203 ways, 0 relations) on overpass-api.de, 269 on kumi, which also 502'd on first hit.

Smaller PARTIALs: NAICS is 2,125 data rows not 2,126 (header counted); taginfo's rp= parameter is ignored so keys/all returned 749 not 200 and combinations returned 464 not 15; category_map.yaml has 67 mappings not ~90; the FSQ HF repo is gated (files 401, and the gate lets Foursquare use your employer name/logo in marketing); the present_in CHECK is in schema_wave2.sql not schema_phase2.sql; the NJ count shipped with no URL.

Biggest miss, and it cuts both ways: "license unknown" for NY/NJ is wrong. OPEN-NY's Terms of Use explicitly waive attribution, share-alike and pre-approval and permit commercial reuse (but grant only a revocable licence — not CC0). NJ legal Section F is similarly permissive. And data.ny.gov nhjr-rpi2 (54,563 licensed DMV facilities, name/street/ZIP/county/georeference) supersedes both datasets cited — while independently confirming the thesis, since none of its 21 business_type codes is truck-specific.

The two load-bearing judgements — NAICS cannot separate truck from car repair, and OSM verdicts must not be persisted into core.businesses — both verified verbatim against source and should be kept.
